punchline: A tiny island killed every one of its pigs on purpose, and outlasted a bigger island that kept cutting trees.
thirty_sec: Jared Diamond sets two Pacific islands side by side. On Easter Island people cut the forest down, partly for giant statues, and the soil washed away and canoes could no longer be built. On tiny Tikopia, under five square kilometres, islanders killed all their pigs, which were wrecking the gardens, and limited their own numbers. The limit was similar, the choice was not: one society gave up something it valued early.
